discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator. It has helical edge states protected by a new Z2 invariant, and Kane and collaborators extended it to three-dimensional topological insulators. Molenkamp's group gave decisive proof in 2007 in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells: quantized edge conductance appeared exactly at the predicted critical thickness, followed by nonlocal transport measurements. This is the model for how a clean theoretical idea becomes a new, measurable state of matter. It established topological band theory as a central organising principle of condensed matter physics, gave rise to topological superconductivity and Majorana proposals as well as higher-order topological phases, and opened routes towards topologically protected quantum information. Its impact is broad, lasting and experimentally unambiguous.
